summary: Iteration 4 — Backend-only verification of the RUT async-submit refactor (fast foreground POST + heavy prep moved to BackgroundTasks). All 26 pytest cases passed in 5.4s against the external REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL. The race-condition the user reported on realflow.online ('Network aborted twice + recovery poll failed') is fixed: the job DB record is now inserted IMMEDIATELY (status=queued, preparing=true) before the BG prep task runs, so recovery polling always finds the job.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 12,124 lines — even larger than iter_3 (was 11,951). The new _rut_prepare_and_run helper (~290 lines) is well-structured but should ideally live in a dedicated rut_router.py module alongside the other RUT endpoints. Maintainability concern, not a bug.
Foreground endpoint correctly returns ~100ms; in-memory RUT_JOBS dict + DB upsert happen synchronously before scheduling BackgroundTasks — good ordering, recovery polling will always find the job.
_DUP_IP_CACHE_LOCK (asyncio.Lock at line 3738) correctly prevents a thundering-herd against Mongo when N concurrent jobs trigger cache rebuild. Good defensive design.
BackgroundTasks runs AFTER the response is sent — confirmed working. _rut_prepare_and_run wraps everything in try/except + _mark_failed so a prep crash never leaves the job stuck in 'queued' forever.
Validation order is correct: link 404 → numeric 400 → file-read 400 → paste-emptiness 400 → DB insert. All foreground 400s observed <2s in tests (typically <500ms).
file_bytes is read before BG task is scheduled (UploadFile handles can't outlive the request) — correctly handled at lines 4160-4173.
On bad upload_proxy_id, the BG task flips status='failed' with error_message='Selected proxy upload is empty or not found' within ~3s — verified end-to-end.

context_for_next_testing_agent: RUT submit refactor is fully working. Key learnings: (1) The foreground endpoint at server.py line 4049 inserts the DB row at line 4205 (before BackgroundTasks.add_task at line 4248), so recovery polling will always find the job — this is the fix. (2) Validation order matters: link_id 404 happens BEFORE paste-emptiness 400, so don't expect 400 for missing-proxies if link_id is also wrong (you'll get 404). (3) Foreground response includes proxies/user_agents counts ONLY for paste-mode; upload-mode counts get filled by the BG task asynchronously — the foreground returns 0 for upload counts which is by design. (4) `total` in response is total_clicks for clicks-mode; for conversions-mode it's max_attempts or target_conversions*20. (5) Test file at /app/backend/tests/test_iteration4_rut_async_submit.py — re-run with `pytest backend/tests/test_iteration4_rut_async_submit.py -v`.
rca of the issue: ROOT CAUSE (from user report): The pre-fix POST /api/real-user-traffic/jobs did all of (a) gsheet HTTP fetches, (b) potentially MB-sized Excel parsing, (c) entire-database dup-IP cache rebuild, (d) target-screenshot pHash calculation SYNCHRONOUSLY before inserting the job row in MongoDB. On Cloudflare-tunneled production with slow uploads, the request frequently exceeded the user's HTTP timeout. The frontend's recovery polling (which lists /jobs and looks for the just-submitted job_id) then found NOTHING because the DB row was never written → 'job DID NOT start' toast. FIX VERIFIED: server.py now (1) does only fast validation in foreground, (2) drains UploadFile bytes (instant — body is already in memory), (3) inserts the job row with status=queued + preparing=true at line 4205, (4) schedules `_rut_prepare_and_run` as a BackgroundTask, (5) returns within ~100ms. Heavy prep runs after response. On any prep failure, the BG task calls _mark_failed which updates DB status='failed' + error_message, surfaced via the existing job-detail poll. Concurrency stress (5 parallel) completes in ~525ms wall-clock with all 5 distinct job_ids visible in /jobs <1s later — the user's 'concurrent jobs working smoothly' requirement is met.
